title: Formalize source-bound forward recipe dispatch
body:
The selected forward word's `RecipesExact` premise still requires a formal connection to the stored recipe dispatcher. This package proves that connection for the unchanged 24,757-event word, conditional on exactly the 2,888 used child-operator identities. It separately binds all 5,064 relabel descriptors in source order; the dispatcher executes independently supplied operators and source-selected records.

The source/target adapters, residual wrappers and identity cases are discharged by algebra. The child identities, serialized operator denotation, Python/JSON adapter and physical execution remain explicit obligations. This contributes no new numerical recipe audit or selected-frontier change.

Validation: a fresh Lean 4.21.0 run compiled 34 modules in 793.1s, checked 97 blocks and reported 20 theorem/control roots using only `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`. Eight independent Python control groups cover raw-record agreement, missing/duplicate events, stride 712, orientation, helper450's literal `2:999` recipe, rank/token mutations and source corruption. Kernel controls reject four false claims. The default registered replay checks the archived receipt and source bindings; `check_lean.py` performs the fresh proof check.

Package: `research/k8-lean-recipe-dispatch/`. Canonical claim and result: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2703#discussioncomment-19007895.

Credits: PR1781's numerical audit, PR1964's extended-label interpretation, PR2048's used-child audit, PR2378/2422's monomial refinements, and PR2944's complete typed word/codec/source generator. Detailed attribution and exact heads are in the README. Prepared by Sagar Thakrar with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; no independent human review is claimed.
